Test group mean against hypothesized value. MNE: ttest_1samp_no_p. Common for activation vs zero baseline.
Between-group comparison. MNE: ttest_ind_no_p. Assumes normality and equal variance.
Within-subject comparison. Homer3: hmrG_t_paired_contrast. Pre-post, condition A vs B.
Welch's t-test: does not assume equal variances. Use when Levene test is significant.
Test differences among 3+ group means. MNE: f_oneway. Assumes normality and homogeneity of variance.
Within-subject factor with 3+ levels. MNE: f_mway_rm. Apply GG/HF correction for sphericity violations.
Between-subjects x within-subjects factorial design. Tests main effects and interaction.
Two between-subjects factors with interaction. Tests main effects and AxB.
Non-parametric paired test. Alternative to paired t-test when normality violated.
Non-parametric independent test. Tests whether distributions differ.
Non-parametric one-way ANOVA alternative.
Non-parametric repeated measures test. Alternative to RM-ANOVA.
Test normality before parametric tests. Shapiro-Wilk (n<5000), K-S, Anderson-Darling.
Test equal variance assumption. Levene's (robust) or Bartlett's (sensitive to normality).
Post-hoc pairwise after significant ANOVA. Controls FWER.
Post-hoc robust to unequal variances and sample sizes.
Most conservative: adjusted_alpha = alpha / n_tests. Controls FWER.
Controls FDR. Most common in fNIRS. Less conservative than Bonferroni.
Valid under arbitrary dependence. Use when spatial/temporal correlation unknown.
MNE permutation_cluster_test. Non-parametric cluster-based correction. Maris & Oostenveld 2007.
MNE spatio_temporal_cluster_1samp_test. Spatial adjacency-aware clustering.
MNE bootstrap_confidence_interval. Non-parametric CI. No distributional assumptions.
MNE linear_regression. OLS for design matrix analysis. Supports robust SE.
Logistic regression for binary classification. Reports OR, AUC. Common in fNIRS diagnostic.
Cohen's d: standardized mean difference. d=0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large. Hedges g corrects small sample bias.
Proportion of variance explained. eta2 = SS_effect/SS_total. Partial eta2 for multi-factor. Omega2 less biased.
Correlation between binary and continuous. Equivalent to Pearson r.
A priori or post hoc power. Calculate required N or achieved power. Critical for study design.
NBS: permutation test for graph/edge-level inference. Identifies connected significant components. Zalesky et al. 2010.
TFCE: threshold-free inference combining extent and height. Smith & Nichols 2009.
Quantify evidence for H1 vs H0. BF10>10 strong for H1, BF10<0.1 strong for H0.

1D CNN: temporal convolutions over fNIRS time series. Each conv layer extracts local temporal patterns. Reference: >89.57% accuracy for MCI detection. Input: (subjects, channels, time). Output: class probabilities.
2D CNN: spatial-temporal convolutions. Treats channel x time as 2D image. Captures both spatial channel relationships and temporal dynamics.
EEGNet: compact CNN with depthwise and separable convolutions. Very few parameters, good for small fNIRS datasets. Lawhern et al. 2018. F1=filters1, D=depth multiplier, F2=filters2.
ShallowConvNet: temporal + spatial convolution with square activation and average pooling. Schirrmeister et al. 2017. Good baseline for BCI.
LSTM: captures long-range temporal dependencies in fNIRS time series. Gating mechanism prevents vanishing gradients. MODWT-LSTM used for physiological noise filtering (extraction evidence).
GRU: lighter alternative to LSTM with fewer parameters. Similar performance, faster training. Cho et al. 2014.
BiLSTM: forward + backward temporal context. Captures both past and future dependencies. merge_mode: concat or sum.

Transformer: self-attention over fNIRS time steps. Captures global temporal dependencies without recurrence. d_model embedding dim, nhead attention heads. Positional encoding for temporal order. Vaswani et al. 2017.

method_label: Temporal Transformer for fNIRS Brain Decoding
notes: Temporal Transformer: sliding window attention for fNIRS. Window-based processing for long sequences. Channel embedding projects each channel to d_model. Evidence: Transformer-LSTM for Parkinson staging.
CNN-LSTM: CNN extracts local temporal features, LSTM models sequential dependencies. Best of both worlds. CNN front-end reduces sequence length for LSTM.
CNN-Transformer: CNN feature extraction + Transformer attention. Captures local patterns and global dependencies.
VAE: learns compact latent representation of fNIRS data. Useful for anomaly detection, data augmentation, and unsupervised feature learning. Beta-VAE for disentangled representations.

method_label: Time Series Data Augmentation for fNIRS
notes: Time series augmentation: jittering (add noise), scaling (multiply), time_warping (non-linear变形), cropping (subsequence), permutation (reorder), rotation (channel mixing). Critical for small fNIRS datasets.

Transfer learning: leverage pretrained models (EEG, fMRI, or large fNIRS corpus) for small target datasets. Freeze early layers, fine-tune later layers. Feature extraction mode: train only classifier head.
Bayesian optimization (Optuna) or random search for DL hyperparameters. Tune learning rate, dropout, hidden size, layers. Early stopping prevents overfitting.

GradCAM: gradient-weighted class activation mapping for CNN. SHAP: SHapley Additive exPlanations for any model. Attention weights: from Transformer layers. Essential for neuroscientific interpretation.
Subject-wise CV: ensures no data leakage across subjects. Nested CV: outer loop for performance estimation, inner loop for hyperparameter tuning. Critical for fNIRS BCI.
DL predicts scalp signal from long channels using short channel features. More flexible than linear regression. Evidence: Transformer-based model for fNIRS short-channel prediction.
Domain adaptation: reduce inter-subject variability. DANN (adversarial), MMD (maximum mean discrepancy), CORAL (correlation alignment). Critical for subject-independent BCI.
